task.description: Write test specs and ExUnit test code for lib/letflow/routers/services.ex, lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex, and lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex's new list_all/1, covering REQ-192's full acceptance-criteria list (see lib/letflow/design/req192-service-catalog-routes.md AC1-AC10 and the design's per-section result-mapping tables) with mutation-driven coverage, not one test per acceptance criterion restated.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/services returns entries visible to the caller's own tenant (global + own-tenant), confirmed by a test with at least one global entry, one own-tenant entry, and one other-tenant entry all present, asserting the response includes exactly the first two

GET /api/v1/admin/services returns entries the caller's own tenant does not own, demonstrating it is not tenant-filtered (list_all/1's cross-tenant-visibility test, both at the context-module level and the router level)

service_record_json/1's response fields are asserted field by field against a registered entry, explicitly documenting (per design doc SS8 finding 1) that max_retries is excluded from the comparison since it has no backing column
three explicit 403 tests, one per admin write route (POST/PATCH/DELETE /admin/services...), for a caller whose auth_context.roles holds none of :PLATFORM_ADMIN

two 409 tests: DELETE of a service referenced by an ACTIVE definition (service_referenced_by_active_definitions), and PATCH narrowing scope on a service another tenant's ACTIVE definition still references (service_scope_narrowing_conflict) -- both asserting the RFC 9457 extensions payload (definition_ids / conflicts) is present and correctly shaped
POST /admin/services with a duplicate service_id returns 409 via plain Response.conflict, and confirms no row was modified

a cursor minted by GET /services (SC: prefix) is rejected with 400 'invalid cursor' when replayed against GET /admin/services, and vice versa a cursor minted by GET /admin/services (SCA: prefix) is rejected when replayed against GET /services -- INV-9 cross-endpoint isolation, at the router level
GET /admin/services with a caller holding only :PLATFORM_ADMIN succeeds (200) and its response body includes rows from more than one tenant
auth_method (request body) -> required_auth (response field) translation is confirmed round-trip via POST then a subsequent read
PATCH/DELETE on a nonexistent service_id returns 404 with no cross-tenant-disguise distinction (design SS10 -- 404 on admin routes means only 'no such id exists')
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
